title: A 158-Year-Old Bank Died in One Weekend #shorts
description:
In September 2008, Lehman Brothers, a bank that had survived the Civil War and the Great Depression, filed the biggest bankruptcy in American history.
Follow for more stories of fortunes lost overnight.
hook_text:
A 158-YEAR-OLD BANK
DIED IN ONE WEEKEND
first_comment: Should the government have saved Lehman? Or was letting it fail the right call? 👇

lines.text: It survived the Civil War, and the Great Depression.
Lehman Brothers was one hundred fifty eight years old.
By 2008, it was the fourth biggest investment bank in America.
But it had bet everything on one thing: American houses.
When homeowners stopped paying, those bets turned toxic.
The bank owed more than six hundred billion dollars.
On one Sunday in September, rivals met to save it.
Nobody would take the risk, and the government said no.
At dawn, Lehman filed for bankruptcy.
Six hundred thirty nine billion dollars in assets, the biggest bankruptcy in history.
The Dow fell five hundred four points that day.
Employees walked out carrying their lives in cardboard boxes.
And the whole world's banks began to fall.
Follow for more stories of fortunes lost overnight.
